title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Topic Models with High-Quality Document Representations
task: Improving generalisation of neural topic models through flatter minima
problem: Neural topic models optimise complex objectives (likelihood plus regularisers) with standard optimisers, ignoring loss-landscape sharpness.
architecture: DREAM optimiser: Friendly-SAM updates for inference-network parameters; the sharpness neighbourhood radius is set from the optimal-transport distance between document-topic distributions and document-cluster proportions obtained by clustering PLM embeddings (stella_en_400M_v5, UMAP, HDBSCAN); applied to ETM, ECRTM, NeuroMax and FASTopic.

datasets.name: GoogleNews
datasets.details: titles of over 10,000 news articles, 152 clusters

key_results: YahooAnswers K = 50: FASTopic Purity 0.589 to 0.641 and NMI 0.353 to 0.391 with DREAM.
GoogleNews K = 100: ECRTM Purity 0.342 to 0.653 and NMI 0.491 to 0.776 with DREAM.
TD often drops (e.g. ECRTM 20NG K = 50: 0.964 to 0.855).
strengths: Optimiser-level improvement that plugs into several NTMs; largest gains on short, noisy texts.
Ablation separates F-SAM from the OT-based radius.

limitations.text: Depends on the quality of the pre-trained clustering, which limits use in continuous/streaming settings.
Topic diversity is lower than the original models in many settings.

notes: Baseline numbers for standard datasets taken from Pham et al. (NeuroMax).
